intent: Return to the iteration 1 best geometry (mass 0.8 kg, wheel_track 0.12 m, 12 mm sensors on the widened row). Changed: mass from 0.7 back to 0.8 kg. Kept: sensor row, sensor size, wheel track, wheel radius and body, all unchanged. Expected result: oval finish rate about 0.5 to 0.7, oval steering_oscillation near 0.26, and a score near 300. This race also tests whether the iteration 1 result is repeatable. I am not considering any further sensor, track or mass change unless this race shows a clear regression.
learning: Iteration 5 showed that the mass-finish relationship is not monotonic (0.6 kg gave 0.30, 0.7 kg gave 0.15, 0.8 kg gave 0.70). Either the 0.7 kg point is noise or the oval finish rate depends on seed variance more than geometry. If this race reproduces about 0.7 finishes at 0.8 kg, the iteration 1 geometry is a stable reference. If it falls well below 0.5, the earlier result was partly seed luck, and future changes should be judged against a multi-seed average rather than a single race.
rationale: Iteration 5 (mass 0.7 kg) scored 185.49, with oval finish rate 0.15. That is below both the 0.6 kg result (0.30) and the 0.8 kg reference (0.70), so the mass-finish relationship is not monotonic. The Integrator's rule covers this case: when the 0.7 kg finish rate stays near 0.3 or below, return to 0.8 kg, the best known mass, and do not try a lower mass again. The 0.7 kg result is treated as noise or a non-monotonic region, not as evidence for a new optimum. Iterations 2 (16 mm sensors) and 3 (0.10 m track) both hurt the oval, so both stay reverted. I am therefore reproducing the iteration 1 geometry exactly: the widened 12 mm row at x = -0.024 to +0.024 m, y = 0.04 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.16 m, mass 0.8 kg. I did not take the Integrator's earlier suggestions to move sensors forward or change body width, because the evidence does not support them. The Integrator's controller is also tuned to this geometry, so holding it unchanged keeps the integration stable. I expect the oval finish rate to return to about 0.5 to 0.7, with a mean score near 300 and wide seed variance (oval scores range 276 to 957 in iteration 1). The s-bend and slalom are unlikely to complete under this geometry, and their off-track limit is near 0.064 m max error. The main uncertainty is whether iteration 1's 0.70 finish rate was partly seed luck, so this race also checks whether the reference is repeatable.
